findings.statement: In v1, scallions are thinly sliced on a cutting board, and parsley is finely chopped with straight knife motions.
In v1, sliced or rolled parsley and scallions are placed into a food processor, and the resulting chopped vegetables or herbs are mixed with bulgur.
In the observed v2 spans, vegetable salad ingredients are already chopped or diced in bowls or measuring cups and are poured, handled, or mixed into a salad bowl.

The visible difference is that v1 shows active knife cutting and food-processor handling of vegetable ingredients, whereas the observed v2 spans show pre-prepared vegetable ingredients being added and mixed.
In v2, a spoon is used for mixing salad contents rather than for cutting or chopping vegetables.

open_questions.question: Whether v2 contains any active vegetable cutting, chopping, or processing outside the observed ingredient-handling and mixing spans remains undetermined.
The exact role of the food processor in v1, including whether it processes all vegetable ingredients or only selected herbs and scallions, remains undetermined.
The comparable vegetable sets prepared by each video remain undetermined from current evidence.

turns.answer: Video A (v1) shows more hands-on vegetable preparation: scallions are sliced on a cutting board, parsley is chopped, and the herbs/scallions are then handled in a food processor before being mixed with bulgur. Video B (v2), in the observed ingredient-handling and mixing spans, shows vegetables already chopped or diced—such as red bell peppers, leafy greens, tomatoes, cucumbers, green onions, and parsley—being poured, handled, and mixed with a spoon; no active cutting or processing is visible in those spans. Thus, the main difference is that Video A depicts active knife and food-processor preparation of vegetable/herb ingredients, whereas Video B depicts assembly and mixing of pre-prepared vegetable ingredients, though Video B’s unobserved portions cannot be fully ruled out.
